articles.title: Sword, Slogan and Arrest: Karni Sena Leader Jailed in Aligarh for Allegedly Inciting Religious Hatr
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Aligarh (UP): Police in Aligarh have arrested Sachin Raghav, a local leader associated with a cow protection group and Karni Sena, for allegedly making objectionable and provocative remarks targeting a religious community. He has been sent to jail following the registration of a case.

body.html:
Aligarh (UP): Police in Aligarh have arrested Sachin Raghav, a local leader associated with a cow protection group and Karni Sena, for allegedly making objectionable and provocative remarks targeting a religious community. He has been sent to jail following the registration of a case.

The action came after a video went viral on social media in which Raghav was seen holding a sword and sporting a twirled moustache, while raising a controversial slogan during a programme at Ghantaghar, where he was garlanding the statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. The slogan, styled on Netaji’s famous call, was alleged by police to have incited religious frenzy.

Taking cognisance of the viral video and related social media posts, the Civil Lines police station registered FIR No. 58/26 under Sections 196(1), 351(2), 353(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 67(A) of the IT Act for making indecent and inflammatory comments online.

CO-III Sarvam Singh said the accused was arrested for promoting religious hatred and disturbing communal harmony. The police team from Civil Lines arrested Sachin Raghav on Thursday from the Bannadevi police station area.

The accused has been identified as Sachin Raghav, son of Tejveer Singh Raghav, a resident of Palda Jhal village, Shikarpur police station, Bulandshahr district, and currently residing at Maharana Pratap Enclave, Swarn Jayanti Nagar, Quarsi, Aligarh.

The arrest was carried out by a police team led by Inspector Sanjeev Kumar, along with Head Constable Vikesh Kumar of Civil Lines police station. Further legal proceedings are underway.

articles.title: “Drive Slow or Drop Me”: Passenger Assaulted by Speeding Bus Driver at Trichy New Bus Stand
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing incident was reported from Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) on the morning of January 30, 2026, where a passenger was allegedly abused and assaulted by a private bus driver after objecting to rash and dangerous driving.

body.html:
A disturbing incident was reported from Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) on the morning of January 30, 2026, where a passenger was allegedly abused and assaulted by a private bus driver after objecting to rash and dangerous driving.

According to the complaint, a private bus named ‘Shankar’ was travelling from the old bus stand to the new bus stand around 7 am. The driver was reportedly driving at a very high speed and in a reckless manner, putting passengers at risk.

Concerned for his safety, one of the passengers warned the driver and conductor, saying, “Don’t drive so fast, or drop me down and let me go.” However, instead of slowing down, the driver allegedly continued driving dangerously on purpose, despite repeated objections from the passenger.

Upon reaching the new Trichy bus stand, the situation escalated. The driver allegedly used obscene and abusive language against the passenger and physically assaulted him. The incident was captured on video by another person present at the spot.

The victim later obtained the video footage and filed a complaint at the police station, submitting details of the incident along with the bus registration number. Police have taken note of the complaint and further action is expected.

The video of the assault has since surfaced on social media, drawing public outrage over passenger safety and the conduct of private bus staff.

articles.title: Moving Bullet in Child’s Head: KGMU Doctors Pull Off Life-Saving Miracle in Lucknow
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Doctors at King George’s Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, have given a new lease of life to a three-year-old girl by successfully removing a revolver bullet lodged in her head through a highly complex surgery.

body.html:
Doctors at King George’s Medical University (KGMU), Lucknow, have given a new lease of life to a three-year-old girl by successfully removing a revolver bullet lodged in her head through a highly complex surgery.

The child, Laxmi, was injured on December 17 while playing on the rooftop of her house in Bastauli village. According to her family, a sudden loud sound was heard, after which her head began bleeding. She was initially taken to a private hospital, where her wound was stitched. However, her condition worsened later that night.

Laxmi’s father, Ramesh, said they rushed her to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, where doctors detected a bullet lodged in her head. Due to the unavailability of beds, she was referred to the KGMU Trauma Centre, where she was admitted in critical condition.

A CT scan revealed that the bullet inside the child’s head was moving, changing its position every few seconds, making the surgery extremely risky. The girl was unconscious and bleeding heavily, and her condition continued to deteriorate.

A specialised medical team was immediately formed under the leadership of Dr BK Ojha, Head of the Neurosurgery Department. The team included five senior neurosurgeons, along with expert paediatricians and anaesthesiologists. To prevent the bullet from shifting further, doctors inserted nine needles simultaneously to stabilise it before proceeding with surgery.

After a four-and-a-half-hour-long operation, the doctors successfully removed the bullet. The child was kept in the ICU for about a week and remained under close observation.

Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Dr Ankur Bajaj of the Neurosurgery Department said the girl was brought to the Trauma Centre in a very critical condition and that operating on a moving bullet was one of the most challenging aspects of the case.

Nearly 40 days after the surgery, Laxmi’s condition has improved significantly, and doctors said she is expected to be discharged within the next two days.

Dr Bajaj added that the girl’s family belongs to a poor financial background, and NGOs assisted in her treatment. Remarkably, the total cost of her treatment was less than ₹40,000.

Meanwhile, police investigating the incident found a bullet mark on the tin shed on the rooftop. Inquiries in nearby houses revealed that no one possessed a licensed firearm, leaving the source of the bullet a mystery. Police said the investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Wrong-Side Driving Sparks Violence: Delhi Tourists Clash With Locals in Uttarakhand’s Srinagar
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A clash broke out between Delhi tourists and local youths in Srinagar town of Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, after an argument over wrong-side driving on the Badrinath National Highway.

body.html:
A clash broke out between Delhi tourists and local youths in Srinagar town of Pauri Garhwal district, Uttarakhand, after an argument over wrong-side driving on the Badrinath National Highway. The situation escalated to such an extent that police had to resort to a mild lathi charge to disperse an agitated crowd.

According to police, the incident began when tourists travelling in two vehicles allegedly overtook local scooter riders from the wrong direction, leading to a heated exchange. The argument soon turned violent near an SBI bank, with abuses and physical scuffles reported.

As the clash intensified, more locals gathered at the spot and later outside the Srinagar Kotwali police station, demanding action against the tourists. Some locals allegedly attempted to pull the tourists out of their vehicles, further escalating tensions.

Police intervened promptly and used mild force to control the crowd and restore order. Srinagar Kotwali in-charge Kuldeep Singh led the operation, ensuring the situation was brought under control without any major injuries.

In connection with the incident, seven individuals were arrested, including six from Delhi—Ajay Ubas, Abhishek Kaushik, Vipin Mandrawal (resident of Dehradun), Vishal Vats, Aakash Dabas, Sagar, and Manish. The two vehicles involved in the incident were also seized. A case has been registered, and the accused were produced before a court.

Police said the situation is now peaceful, and additional vigilance has been imposed in the area to prevent any further disturbance.

articles.title: Joke Turns Fatal? Young Model Found Dead After Family Tiff in Lucknow
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A aspiring model, Tanu Singh (28), was found dead at her residence in Indiranagar, Lucknow, on Wednesday evening, in an apparent s**cide case. Tanu, a resident of Lakdar Mandi in Saadatganj, had married Rahul Srivastava, an auto driver from Takrohi, four years ago in a love marriage.

body.html:
A aspiring model, Tanu Singh (28), was found dead at her residence in Indiranagar, Lucknow, on Wednesday evening, in an apparent s**cide case.

Tanu, a resident of Lakdar Mandi in Saadatganj, had married Rahul Srivastava, an auto driver from Takrohi, four years ago in a love marriage. On Wednesday afternoon, Tanu was at home with her husband, sister-in-law Anjali, and their young son. During light-hearted banter, Rahul and Anjali allegedly made a remark mocking Tanu, which reportedly hurt her.

Upset, Tanu went into another room and locked the door from inside. About an hour later, when the family called her for dinner and received no response, Anjali looked through a window and found Tanu hanging from a ceiling fan using a dupatta.

She was immediately taken to Lohia Hospital with the help of locals, where doctors declared her brought dead. Police reached the spot, conducted a postmortem, and handed over the body to the family.

Police officials said preliminary findings point to a domestic dispute arising from a joke. No written complaint has been filed so far. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Drunk to Enforce the Law? UP PRV Cops Caught Intoxicated, Torch Mistaken for Liquor Bottle
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident involving allegedly intoxicated police personnel has come to light from Jalaun district in Uttar Pradesh, where a PRV (Police Response Vehicle) team sent to handle a dispute was itself found drunk.

body.html:
A shocking incident involving allegedly intoxicated police personnel has come to light from Jalaun district in Uttar Pradesh, where a PRV (Police Response Vehicle) team sent to handle a dispute was itself found drunk. One of the policemen was seen mistaking a torchlight for a liquor bottle and putting it to his mouth, a moment captured on video that has since gone viral on social media.

The incident occurred in Babina village under the Kadaura police station area, where the PRV team had reportedly arrived to pacify a drunken man and resolve a land dispute between two brothers. However, instead of calming the situation, the police personnel allegedly escalated it.

According to eyewitnesses, the police team was heavily intoxicated and brutally assaulted a drunk youth at the spot. During the episode, a visibly exhausted policeman was seen attempting to drink alcohol, mistakenly lifting a flashlight to his mouth, while another policeman stood nearby and appeared to assist the inebriated individual.

Women present at the scene recorded the incident on their mobile phones. The videos later surfaced on social media, triggering widespread outrage and raising serious questions about police conduct.

Responding to the incident, Jalaun Police stated that the matter has been taken seriously. Officials said that the Circle Officer (CO) Kalpi has been directed to conduct an investigation and take necessary action against those found guilty.

Further action is awaited based on the outcome of the inquiry.

articles.title: ‘Stop Signal Turned Into Horror’: Speeding Car Drags Traffic Cop 500 Metres in Greater Noida,
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident was reported from Greater Noida on January 27, where a traffic police constable was dragged on the bonnet of a speeding car after the driver ignored signals to stop. The incident occurred at the Sector P3 roundabout amid heavy traffic congestion.

body.html:
A shocking incident was reported from Greater Noida on January 27, where a traffic police constable was dragged on the bonnet of a speeding car after the driver ignored signals to stop.

The incident occurred at the Sector P3 roundabout amid heavy traffic congestion. Traffic constable Gurmeet Chaudhary was on duty regulating traffic when a red Hyundai i20 approached the roundabout at high speed. Despite repeated signals to stop, the driver allegedly accelerated and rammed into the constable.

To avoid being run over, Chaudhary landed on the car’s bonnet. The vehicle continued to speed, dragging him for nearly 500 metres, before slowing down and throwing him onto the roadside. The driver then fled the spot.

The injured constable was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was treated for injuries. Police said his condition is stable and he is out of danger.

Based on Chaudhary’s complaint, an FIR has been registered at Beta-2 police station under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including rash and negligent driving, assault on a public servant, and attempt to murder.

Police officials said CCTV footage from the area is being analysed to trace the vehicle. Three police teams have been formed to identify and arrest the accused driver. No arrest had been made till January 28.

A video of the incident, reportedly shot by a passerby, has gone viral on social media, triggering widespread outrage.

articles.title: Family Dragged Out of Car, Brutally Beaten in Hardoi; Village Head’s Husband Among Accused
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video from Hardoi district, Uttar Pradesh, has triggered widespread outrage after showing a family being forcibly stopped on the road, dragged out of their car, and brutally assaulted by a mob allegedly led by the village head’s husband.

body.html:
A disturbing video from Hardoi district, Uttar Pradesh, has triggered widespread outrage after showing a family being forcibly stopped on the road, dragged out of their car, and brutally assaulted by a mob allegedly led by the village head’s husband.

The incident took place in Kachhuna village, where the victims—including a woman advocate, her husband, and her brother-in-law—were attacked in broad daylight. The viral video shows the car being blocked mid-road, after which around a dozen men armed with sticks and iron rods surround the vehicle and assault the occupants.

In the footage, the male victims are seen being beaten so severely that one collapses to the ground, yet the attackers continue to strike him. The woman advocate is also chased and beaten as she tries to escape. Her screams and the attackers’ threats are clearly audible in the video.

Dispute and Allegations

According to the complaint, the violence stemmed from a dispute between Mohammad Naseem, husband of the village head, and Salim, a resident of Takiya. The conflict allegedly escalated, leading to a planned attack on the advocate’s family, reportedly carried out at the village headman’s behest. The complainant has also alleged that threats were issued to deter any protest.

Police Action

Based on the woman advocate’s complaint, police have registered a case under serious sections against 12 named accused, including Mohammad Naseem, along with 50–60 unidentified persons.

Hardoi ASP Subodh Kumar Gautam stated that the accused are being identified using the viral video footage and that efforts are underway to arrest those involved.

The incident has once again raised concerns over lawlessness, misuse of power, and mob violence in rural areas, with many demanding swift and strict action against the accused.
